data.title: Chat: the AS-98 href allowlist guard misses compound assignment (||=, ??=, &&=) on a new anchor

data.body: Filed from the AS-98 QA review (finding F1, agent:qa-priya, 2026-09-11, at head 156faa5); re-filed from AS-119 (cancelled) to carry the Chat set's critical priority. OBSERVED, not argued: a new anchor in app.js doing 'p1.href ||= task.taskId' survives every AS-93/AS-98 guard (link-sites.test.js and the api.test.js link-site tests: 67/67 green). Cause: HREF_ASSIGN only recognises '=' and '+=', and MECHANISMS bans only '.href +=', so '||=' / '??=' / '&&=' are invisible to T8 (allowlist) and T9 (mechanism ban), and the href-assignment count pin never increments. Narrowed by Priya's probe P8: the same operator on an EXISTING site IS red {T7, T8} via the count going 9 -> 8, so only a fresh element evades. Priya judged it not an honest-mistake spelling and deliberately did not apply the fix inline because it changes guard behaviour. Proposed close (one regex): add the compound operators to MECHANISMS (a pattern matching .href followed by ||= or ??= or &&=), or widen HREF_ASSIGN to admit compound operators so the count pin and allowlist both see them; with an anchored mutant re-running P8-on-a-new-anchor and observing red. complexity: low; test-only guard tightening; joins the tail of the Chat-set age queue. Note for the planner: AS-115 (click-to-copy chips, in needs_human at 124440b) adds test/copy-refs.test.js with its own whitespace-insensitive href-assignment count pin over app.js; keep the two pins consistent.
